Ten winners on the stage at Stockholm City Hall last evening. Two from India. Both from the Social Alpha portfolio.

I was in the room, and it was a privilege to watch CanvaLoop and Microbeworks Scientific stand alongside the world’s most promising textile innovators. The same hall hosts the Nobel Prize banquet every year :)

This award doesn’t celebrate ideas. It celebrates science on the hard road from lab to market: the lab, the pilot line, the supply chain and the sceptics. Some of these teams have made it down that road. Others are being de-risked for it right now.

The textile industry will not decarbonise through pledges and panels. It will decarbonise through new fibres, new chemistry, new biology and new processes that work at the scale of India’s mills and MSME clusters. That is where the hard problems live, and that is where Indian deep science now competes on equal terms.

Our job has always been simple to state and hard to do: find the science, de-risk it, and take it to deployment. Days like this remind us that patient, early risk capital pays off in places conventional markets ignore.

Congratulations to all the founders and teams, and thank you, H&M Foundation, for recognising them.

India is not just a market for the textile transition. It will be one of its engines.

Discussions focused on GIFT IFSC as a competitive gateway for cross-border capital, backed by its regulatory sandbox, incentives and world-class infrastructure.

The team also participated in a Gujarat Chamber of Commerce & Industry (GCCI) roundtable organised by its NRG Taskforce in collaboration with the Gujarat State Non-Resident Gujaratis' Foundation. The session featured Vitasta Kaul Vyas, Chairperson, NRG Taskforce, GCCI, and Pruthvi Patel, Co-Chairperson, NRG Taskforce, GCCI. Some partnerships take time to deliver. Others don’t.
Our partnership with Tech incubator iCreate (based in Ahmedabad, Gujarat) is clearly in the second category.

It was signed by iCreate CEO Avinash Punekar and our then regional Vice-Président François Decoster (now Ambassador to New-Zealand!) on 11th June this year in Lille, as part of our European AI Summit led by our regional president Xavier Bertrand.

4 months later, here I am in Ahmedabad, meeting our partners, and taking part in a roundtable of startups, identifying how they could deploy their technologies in Europe, using the Region Hauts-de-France as a natural gateway. 

Why so quickly and with some concrete actions and plans already in place? 

Largely because of our alignement in expectations, networks, motivation and key interests: DeepTech, semi-conductors, drones, Space, BioTech, MedTech, AI and advanced computing.

This is even more fruitful as we provide access to our respective ecosystems. 

I had the chance of meeting up with:
➡️ GIFT City: India’s massive and ambitious International Financial and Technological centre - an Indian version of Hong Kong or Singapore.
➡️ Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Gandhinagar: one of the 23 IITs in India, one of the most advanced and respected DeepTech research networks in the world.
➡️ Gujarat Government Tech networks and initiatives, such as iHub ind
➡️ Gujarat Chamber of Commerce and Industry, who organised a live discussion with 50 companies eager to explore EU market access

It’s hard to have a more packed and fruitful agenda over 36 hours in Ahmedabad! 

Many thanks to Avinash Punekar Siddharth Pareek and the iCreate team for all the efforts, looking forward to build on all these actions and projects!

What does it take for Indian deep tech startups to access European markets? Conversations like these are where new possibilities begin.

iCreate welcomed Mr Artus Galiay, Director, Nord France Invest, UK, Ireland and India, for an interaction with the iCreate team and portfolio startups to explore opportunities for cross-border collaboration and expansion into France and the wider European market.

The engagement was part of the India–Hauts-de-France Deep Tech Innovation Corridor, established under the MoU signed between iCreate and the Hauts-de-France Regional Council in June 2026 at Bharat Innovates, Nice. The corridor aims to create pathways for market access, industry partnerships, research collaboration and pilot deployments between the two regions.

Discussions covered the industrial strengths of Hauts-de-France, the support offered by Nord France Invest to Indian companies, and opportunities emerging through the corridor. Portfolio startups pitched their innovations and participated in one-to-one discussions with Mr Galiay, exploring potential collaborations, market entry strategies and expansion opportunities in France and Europe.

The session concluded with an interactive networking dinner, offering further opportunities to exchange ideas, build connections and explore avenues for future collaboration.

Through this initiative, iCreate continues to strengthen international partnerships and create new pathways for deep tech startups to access global markets.
